textos: Why does this Soviet sanatorium stand on just three legs?
Built by Igor Vasilevsky between 1978 and 1985: a thermal spa for Soviet oil workers.
Druzhba means friendship: a joint project of the USSR and Czechoslovakia.
Every notch is a room with a sea view, and part of the structure.
You come in from the top: across a bridge, onto the roof.
Lifts inside the legs take guests down to the rooms and to the sea.
The real reason is underneath: a slope prone to landslides, in seismic zone 8.
Three supports, and a ring that flies over the hillside instead of sitting on it.
Legend says Turkish spies took it for a secret military base.
